notes:
Context: SMB, self-serve trial. Primary product: hosted API (public cloud only). Use case = support bot + doc search; expected traffic currently small but spiky during product launches. Customer observed: repeated 'request timeout' errors for chat users midday; p95 latency ~1.2-1.4s in their reports. They say: "Feels like half our chats stall for a few seconds then recover". Behavior is reproducible in their EU-based tests but not always in our region.

SE observations / quick wins recommended: 
- Region choice: customer is NA-heavy but runs tests from EU. Recommend switching to nearest region to user base (us-east-1 or us-west-2) for low-latency front-end -> backend hop. Suggest they run a fast A/B: same request from eu-west-1 vs us-west-2 and capture p50/p95.
- Timeouts: their client SDK used default 30s but browser front-end enforced 10s. Recommend setting client read timeout to 15s and server retry policy 1 retry with jitter to avoid retry storms. Document: drive://redwood/perf-tuning-checklist-2026
- Prompt length: large system prompts + long chat history add ~200-800 tokens. Advise template-based system prompt + truncate older messages (LRU) — aim to keep input tokens < 1k for chat flows. Provide example: compress user history via summarization before sending full context.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: encourage streaming for perceived latency (first-byte) even if overall generation time similar. For short responses (<60 tokens) non-streaming okay.
- Batching & caching: not yet applicable (low QPS) but enable prefix caching for repeated FAQ queries once moving to Dedicated.
- Model selection: recommend trying 8k token model variant with quantization-friendly variant for cost/latency tradeoff; advise testing 'redwood-4c-8k-quant' in target region.
- SDK config: increase socket keepalive, enable http/2 when possible, and use our client-side connection pooling hints.

Customer quotes / color: "If we could get p95 under 500ms for typical FAQ hits we'd be happy to convert trial". They are cost-sensitive but will pay modest monthly if UX fixes latency.
